answer: Counterfactual-dependence audit: each answer seals a map naming its key premises and predicting how the verdict shifts if any one is flipped. At settlement the ledger flips one premise and graders check the forecast. An author who grasps the causal chain writes this cheaply — knowing damming the inlet, breaching the jetty, or a surging glacier reroutes water differently. A farm refilling a template with those words has a conclusion depending on no premise, so every flip draws the same hollow line and one shared map damns its cloned cluster. Cost: N real causal forecasts, not one shell.
